Here are the answers.

---

**h01** — `s3presign.Runner` (S3 pre-signed URL refresher) — every **12 hours** (`runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`, `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`, ticker at `:30`), plus one immediate pass at boot — wired in `server/server.go:162-171` (`startBackgroundRunners`, called from `Start` at `server/server.go:129`). It re-presigns S3-backed attachments whose URL is within 1 day of its 5-day expiry (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:46-127`).

**h02** — delivery function: `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (actual send at `:148` `safeClient.Do(req)`; async path enqueues via `PostAsync` `:184` consumed by 4 worker goroutines at `:42-54`).
Protection: SSRF guard at dial time — `safeDialContext` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:59`) installed as the shared client's `Transport.DialContext` (`:30-36`); it resolves the host and rejects reserved/private IPs via `isReservedIP` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:44`) against `reservedCIDRs` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:14-23`, incl. 169.254.0.0/16 IMDS). Checking at dial time also defeats DNS rebinding. Registration-time check: `webhook.ValidateURL` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:62`), called from `server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74,161,182`. Escape hatch: `webhook.AllowPrivateIPs` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:41`).

**h03** — abstraction package: `internal/idp` (`internal/idp/idp.go:3` — `IdentityProviderUserInfo`, the provider-neutral user shape); implementation package: `internal/idp/oauth2` (`internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go` — OAuth2/OIDC `IdentityProvider` with `NewIdentityProvider` `:26`, `ExchangeToken` `:45`, used at `server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:121`). OAuth2 is the only concrete protocol implementation shipped.

**h04** — **no**. Evidence: `store/db/mysql` is imported in exactly one file, `store/db/db.go:8` (`grep -rn "usememos/memos/store/db/mysql"` returns only that line), and `mysql.NewDB` is called only at `store/db/db.go:22` inside the `NewDBDriver` switch (`store/db/db.go:14-31`). The only other construction is a literal `&DB{}` in a test, `store/db/mysql/auth_config_test.go:12` (non-production).

**h05** — **explicit Go code**, in each driver's user-delete transaction; there is no DB-level cascade for reactions.
- `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:96` + `:102` → `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx` (`:380`) and `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx` (`:400`)
- `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:96,102` (funcs at `:380`, `:400`)
- `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:96,102` (funcs at `:417`, `:437`)
- Entry: `Store.DeleteUser` (`store/user.go:171`) → `driver.DeleteUser` (e.g. `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:29`), reached from `server/router/api/v1/user_service.go:414` and `auth_service_sso.go:77`.
- Schema check: the `reaction` table has no foreign key / `ON DELETE CASCADE` (`store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:91-98`, `postgres/LATEST.sql:90-97`, `mysql/LATEST.sql:90-97`); the only cascade in the schema is `memo_share.memo_id → memo(id)` (`store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:109`).

**h11** — 1st: **`store.User`** — referenced from ~6 packages outside `store/` (`server/auth`, `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/fileserver`, `server/router/rss`; ~25 files). 2nd: **`store.Memo`** — ~4 packages (`server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/rss`, `server/notification`, `server/runner/memopayload`; ~18 files). **h12** — concrete method: **`(*sqlite.DB).CreateMemo`** — `store/db/sqlite/memo.go:16` (INSERT built at `:41`, executed at `:42`).
Determination: the default `driver` value is `"sqlite"` — `cmd/memos/main.go:122` (`viper.SetDefault("driver", "sqlite")`) and `:130` (flag default); with no `--dsn`, the DSN is derived as `<data>/memos_prod.db` (`internal/profile/profile.go:110-117`). That value flows into `profile.Driver` (`cmd/memos/main.go:43`) → `db.NewDBDriver` (`cmd/memos/main.go:57`), whose `switch profile.Driver` picks `sqlite.NewDB` (`store/db/db.go:19-20`). The call chain is `APIV1Service.CreateMemo` → `Store.CreateMemo` (`store/memo.go:109`) → `s.driver.CreateMemo` (`store/memo.go:113`), i.e. the `store.Driver` interface, so only the injected driver decides among the three candidate `CreateMemo` implementations (`sqlite/memo.go:16`, `postgres/memo.go`, `mysql/memo.go`).

**h13** — impl: the unexported **`markdown.service`** struct — `internal/markdown/markdown.go:58` — the sole implementation of `markdown.Service` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:31`).
Construction: `markdown.NewService(...)` — `internal/markdown/markdown.go:85` — called in production only at `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48-51` with `WithTagExtension()` + `WithMentionExtension()` (also `server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:44` in tests). It wraps a goldmark instance (GFM + custom tag/mention extensions, `markdown.go:91-107`).
Holders of the interface: `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:35`), `RSSService.MarkdownService` (`server/router/rss/rss.go:45`, injected at `server/server.go:85`), and `memopayload.Runner.MarkdownService` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:16`); it's also passed as a parameter to `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`).

Triggers: `CreateMemo` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108`); `UpdateMemo` when the `content` field is in the update mask (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447`); and the bulk backfill `memopayload.Runner.RunOnce` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:52`) — which is currently unwired (see h08).
Extracted: `Tags` (`#tag` nodes, `markdown.go:376-378`) and `Property` — `Title` (leading H1, `:383-389`), `HasLink`, `HasCode`, `HasTaskList`, `HasIncompleteTasks` (`:392-406`). `Mentions` are also extracted in the same pass (used by `server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:32`) but are not stored in the payload. The list/preview `snippet` is derived separately at response-conversion time via `getMemoContentSnippet` → `MarkdownService.GenerateSnippet(content, 64)` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:83-85`, used at `memo_service_converter.go:76`).

---

**r01** — Premise is wrong: there is no Redis anywhere in this repo (no `redis` reference in any Go file or in `go.mod`). Caching is a process-local in-memory cache: `store/cache/cache.go` (`Cache` struct `:66`, `New` `:74`, `Interface` `:11`). Three instances are created in `store.New` — `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` — `store/store.go:51-53`, all sharing one config declared at `store/store.go:39-44`: **DefaultTTL 10 minutes**, cleanup every 5 minutes, MaxItems 1000. So user entries expire 10 minutes after being set (`store/user.go:143`, `:167`), and are explicitly invalidated on user delete (`store/user.go:179`).

**r02** — Premise is wrong: there is no rate-limiting middleware in this codebase. The only Echo middleware registered is `middleware.Recover()` and `newCORSMiddleware(profile)` (`server/server.go:51-52`); no `golang.org/x/time/rate`, no limiter/throttle package in `go.mod` or any Go file. The only mention of the concept is an aspirational comment about email sending (`internal/email/doc.go:86`). Concurrency is bounded instead by semaphores (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:59-60`, `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:117`), which is not per-user rate limiting.

**r03** — Premise is wrong: there is no nightly database-cleanup job and no cron scheduler running in this server. `internal/scheduler` exists as a standalone cron library, but it is imported only from its own tests (`internal/scheduler/integration_test.go:13`, `example_test.go:10`) — never from production code; `"daily-cleanup"` at `"0 2 * * *"` appears only in the README/doc examples (`internal/scheduler/README.md:36-38`, `internal/scheduler/doc.go:15-17`). The only real background job is the S3 presign runner on a plain 12-hour `time.Ticker` (see h01).

**r04** — Premise is wrong: there is no message broker — no NATS, RabbitMQ, AMQP, or Kafka anywhere in the repo (no such imports in `go.mod` or any Go file), and no queue is declared. Webhook delivery is fully in-process: a buffered Go channel `asyncPostQueue` of capacity 128 (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:38`), drained by 4 goroutines started in `init()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-54`), each calling `Post` (`:120`). `PostAsync` (`:184`) does a non-blocking send and **drops** the webhook with a warning when the buffer is full (`:190-195`); nothing is persisted, so pending deliveries are lost on restart.

**r05** — Premise is wrong: there is no GraphQL schema or GraphQL dependency anywhere (no match for "graphql" in Go, `go.mod`, TS, or `package.json`). The public API is **gRPC + Protocol Buffers**, defined in `proto/api/v1/*.proto` (`memo_service.proto`, `user_service.proto`, `auth_service.proto`, `attachment_service.proto`, `idp_service.proto`, `instance_service.proto`, `shortcut_service.proto`, `ai_service.proto`, `common.proto`), generated into `proto/gen/api/v1/`, and exposed over HTTP via grpc-gateway/Connect in `APIV1Service.RegisterGateway` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:64-65`). Additional non-gRPC surfaces: the HTTP file server (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121-125`), RSS (`server/router/rss/rss.go`), and MCP (`server/router/mcp/`, registered at `server/server.go:91-96`).
